title: I Used the Mosque Shoe-Rack Camera on the Volunteer Who Took a Pair

parts.text: I tagged pair 11 at 12:48 p.m. and volunteer Yas took a black pair from the camera cone toward the stair. The card said: TAG THE RACK. CAMERAS ON. NO STAIR PAIRS. I was thirty-three, congregant, holding a tag. Yas shrugged. "Volunteers are the hall." I photographed the card, the tag, and the pair in the cone. Then I asked for the rack log. At 12:54 the board pinged why Yas's name was on a stair pair. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. I have learned the difference between a title and a line item.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The board can see Yas carrying a tagged pair toward the stair on camera.

social.video_title: The volunteer took a tagged pair toward the stair — Part 1/2
social.description: Mosque shoe rack, a camera cone, a pair off the tag. I logged the stair. Would you have asked the board?

parts.text: Yas called it a mix-up until the board asked for the still. I printed the log, the card, and the photo. The pair returned. Yas tagged like everyone else and told the next volunteer mix-ups were always about optics. Optics is a word volunteers use when cones exist. Camera policy now has a second line: STAIRS ARE NOT THE RACK. I keep pair 11. Yas brown-bags the jokes. The hall finally looks like a tag, not a shortcut. If it is written, it can be applied to the person who wrote it.

social.video_title: Stairs are not the rack — Part 2/2
social.description: Rack log, returned pair, and a second line. Was a mix-up ever the stair?
